step: Fair Baseline Step4 - LNLN pre-training audit

data.protocol: LNLN native token/frame-level erase; not CMRP whole-modality Protocol B

selection_metric.code_behavior: Per-metric best checkpoint, with metric-specific comparisons

validation_behavior.role: diagnostic/in-memory tracking; not the source of saved best checkpoints

selection_audit.finding: The official training code uses test metrics to update and save metric-specific best checkpoints.
selection_audit.leakage_caveat: This is test-driven checkpoint selection. It is not a clean validation-selected reproduction protocol.
selection_audit.recommended_reporting: Report native official-code reproduction with an explicit test-selection caveat; do not call it validation-selected or leak-free. A clean validation-selected rerun would be a separate protocol and must not overwrite native results.

readme_paper_consistency.README: README states that checkpoints are selected as best-performing separately for each metric type and warns that metrics can correspond to different epochs.
readme_paper_consistency.paper_context: Robust evaluation loads best_{metric}_{seed}.pth and averages results over missing rates r=0.0,...,0.9.
readme_paper_consistency.assessment: Metric-specific checkpoint selection is consistent with the README wording; the implementation's test-driven selection is an additional methodological caveat not made explicit there.

actual_code_config.training_missing_generation: Each modality receives per-sample U(0,1) missing rates; half of samples per modality are forced to rate 0; text erases tokens to UNK=100 and audio/vision erase frames to zero.
actual_code_config.eval_missing_generation: Uniform scalar missing_rate_eval_test is applied to all three modalities; robust_evaluation sweeps 0.0 through 0.9.
actual_code_config.model_selection: Test-driven per-metric checkpoint saving; validation is tracked but not saved.

phase2_audit_comparison.model_selection: Phase-2 recorded per-metric caveat but did not explicitly identify test-driven checkpoint saving; code audit adds this caveat
phase2_audit_comparison.scheduler: newly verified from source: warmup + cosine annealing

environment.local_assessment: CPU-only; do not run official 200-epoch reproduction locally

smoke_reference.note: Smoke proves official data and code path run; it is not paper evidence and uses a different batch size/epoch count from the official config.

estimated_runtime.cpu_linear_reference: About 61.8 hours per seed if naively extrapolating 3338.2 seconds for 3 smoke epochs; this is not a reliable official-config estimate because smoke used batch_size=8 and num_workers=0.
estimated_runtime.gpu_estimate: No local GPU is available, so no measured speedup exists. For an A40-class or similar CUDA server, plan roughly 2-8 hours for one 200-epoch MOSI seed, subject to GPU, CUDA/PyTorch compatibility, dataloader behavior, and actual throughput. Treat this as a planning range, not a benchmark.
estimated_runtime.10_epoch_gpu_smoke: Use the measured 10-epoch wall time on the selected server to replace the planning range before starting 200 epochs.
estimated_runtime.memory_requirement: Use an A40-class GPU or another GPU with ample VRAM; verify one official batch before committing to a rental.
